A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VerifyBench and VerifyBench-Hard study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and reformatted material.

before.justification: v3 reports original verifier evaluations, reference-answer ablations, error analyses and downstream RL and rejection sampling fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds downstream verifier comparisons, benchmark distribution analyses and verifier case studies.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, disagreement-based selection, human annotation and binary verification procedures remain unchanged. No new proposed model, training objective or algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 41 source datasets, reasoning domains, four answer types and downstream RL/RFT tasks. The new distributions and illustrative cases document existing coverage rather than establish additional datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: v4 adds math-verify to the RL comparison in Section 5.2 and Figure 3. In RFT, v3's three LLM verifiers become four through adding gpt-oss-20b, alongside a newly evaluated math-verify comparator (v4 Appendix J.2 and Figure 11). The comparator sets in Tables 2–5 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain their metrics, prompts, data counts, base models, training budgets and decoding settings. v4 specifies math-verify v0.8.0, but v3 provides no version, so this disclosure does not establish a protocol change from a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: v4 adds source-model and completion-length analyses in Appendix F and four explicit verifier failure cases in Appendix M. It also extends the existing RL/RFT validation through additional comparators. These supplement the retained reference-answer ablation and fine-grained error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight sampled evaluations per RL test example and sixteen for RFT, with the same averaging and curve-smoothing practices. v4 adds no seeds, independent-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; its new distribution statistics are descriptive.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces math-verify's average accuracy of 45.90% with 66.95% on VerifyBench and 32.50% with 76.00% on VerifyBench-Hard. Since only v4 specifies the library version, these are revised reported results rather than established same-configuration gains. v4 also adds RL/RFT curves, source and length distributions, and case-level judgments. Other Table 2 model scores and Tables 3–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and accuracy formulations in Section 2 retain their substance. Replacing the reward symbol r with reward in Equations 1 and 3 resolves a notation collision without changing the definitions. No theoretical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about reference-based reward evaluation, the challenging benchmark variant and practical relevance to reasoning-model training. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets source-model balance and completion-length diversity as supporting benchmark coverage and realism. Appendix M frames displayed disagreements as verifier failures, although some supporting labels are problematic. The existing limitations and principal mechanism explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 identifies math-verify v0.8.0 and the veRL remote_rm recipe, and adds a reproducibility statement identifying dataset and evaluation code in supplementary materials. The public access links, substantive training hyperparameters and hardware descriptions were already provided in v3.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. Related work moves from Appendix B to C while retaining the same positioning against preference-based reward benchmarks and the concurrent VerifierBench, including the distinctions in data sources, taxonomy and disagreement-based selection.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v4 adds a contents list, acknowledgements, an LLM usage declaration and a reproducibility statement; reorganizes annotation and example subsections; and makes limited terminology, notation and author/header corrections.

P2.justification: The appendix examples are substantially redesigned from standalone figure panels into subsectioned text boxes, with additional Hard examples and error cases. v4 adds Table 8 and Figure 4, expands RL/RFT plots and legends, resizes prompt panels and relocates Table 5. The new boxes sometimes split awkwardly across pages, including an isolated final label on page 41.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful downstream controls, benchmark distributions and implementation disclosures. However, its new error analysis introduces material inconsistencies: Section 5.1 attributes the cases to gpt-oss-120b while Appendix M names gpt-oss-20b, and Case 2 labels equivalent final expressions False despite the verifier correctly demonstrating equivalence. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an illustration error or reflects an underlying benchmark-label problem. These unresolved reliability concerns prevent a confident net-quality judgment despite the useful additions.
